turns.answer:
Two answers here, with a caveat on the first:

**tamarack-sw weekly traffic:** No data available. obi's stored history (the only source that can report a rate/utilization over a week) only covers the gateway devices — tamarack-sw isn't one of them. I also tried a live SNMP spot-check as a fallback, but tamarack-sw **timed out** — it's not responding to SNMP right now, so I can't get even a current counter reading, let alone a week's trend. Worth checking if tamarack-sw is reachable at all (want me to run `routeros_status` or a ping to it?).

**tamarack-internet-gw busiest interface right now** (from stored history, last hour, 2025-05-29 22:13–23:13 UTC):
- **sfp-sfpplus5-sycamore** is busiest: **306 Mbit/s avg / 368 Mbit/s peak inbound**, ~49 Mbit/s out — this is the primary DOGWOOD2 fiber uplink carrying the bulk of internet traffic.
- sfp-sfpplus1-tamarack-gw (the downstream link to tamarack-gw): 310 Mbit/s avg / 371 Mbit/s peak **outbound**, 49 Mbit/s in — essentially mirroring the fiber traffic being handed off to the site.
- sfp-sfpplus6-spruce (secondary uplink): mostly idle, ~3 Mbit/s in.
- 15 other interfaces idle (0 bit/s).

So the DOGWOOD2 fiber uplink and the tamarack-gw distribution link are running neck-and-neck as the busiest pair, each carrying ~300+ Mbit/s in their dominant direction — consistent with normal primary-uplink traffic flow.
